subject: Clarify: Marketplace invoice recipient for co-sell + VAT handling (EU reverse-charge & US W-9 path)
messages:
From: Rajesh Mehta <rajesh.mehta@acmecorp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Invoice routing for upcoming co-sell (marketplace split & VAT)

Hi Vanessa,

Quick one as we prep the order for next quarter: Acme will be purchasing via AWS Marketplace (co-sell listing). Procurement needs clarity on which legal entity at Redwood will issue the invoice and whether Acme should expect a marketplace invoice (AWS) or a vendor invoice from Redwood. Key asks:

- For EU entities (specifically Acme Europe Ltd., VAT GB123456789), will Redwood issue an invoice net of VAT under reverse-charge, or will AWS invoice and Redwood show a revenue split elsewhere?
- For US entities, does Redwood need a completed W-9 from Acme before we can be invoiced directly, or will AWS handle tax paperwork?
- Any documentation/process for deferred revenue recognition that affects how our finance team should map the invoice?

I've attached a sample invoice our AP team expects; procurement would like a one-page summary of the routing and any forms required so they can close the PO.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Rajesh Mehta
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Corp
procurement@acmecorp.com
Attachment: acme_sample_co-sell_invoice.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Invoice routing for upcoming co-sell (marketplace split & VAT)

Rajesh — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Karthik (billing) and Kimberly (tax/compliance) so we can give definitive answers. High-level: there are two common patterns depending on how the transaction is set up in AWS ("marketplace facilitation" vs "vendor-billed"). I'll outline the path and what we need from Acme.

Karthik, Kimberly — see procurement questions below and attached sample from Rajesh. Can you confirm Redwood's recommended routing and required paperwork for both EU reverse-charge and US W-9? Also advise if this impacts our revenue recognition (deferred revenue) mapping for the deal id HS-82319.

- EU (Acme Europe Ltd.): if the purchase is listed as "Marketplace purchase" (AWS invoices Acme directly), AWS typically issues the invoice and applies marketplace VAT rules. In that case, Redwood receives a payout from AWS and should supply evidence for VAT reverse-charge in our records, but Acme will not receive a vendor invoice from Redwood. If instead this is a vendor-billed configuration, Redwood will invoice Acme directly net of VAT under reverse-charge (we need their VAT number and a signed EU VAT self-assessment on the PO).

- US (Acme US Inc.): if marketplace invoices, then AWS handles tax. If vendor-billed, we need a completed W-9 on file.

I'll wait for Karthik/Kimberly to confirm exact doc names and whether a DocuSign sign-off is required for the EU self-assessment.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Cloud Channel Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Rajesh Mehta <rajesh.mehta@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Invoice routing for upcoming co-sell (marketplace split & VAT)

Vanessa, Rajesh — on the billing side I've reviewed the AWS listing setup for HS-82319. Short answers:

1) Routing: This deal is configured as an AWS-facilitated marketplace sale for EU customers by default. That means:
   - AWS will issue the invoice to Acme Europe Ltd. and handle VAT collection/placement per their marketplace rules.
   - Redwood will receive a payout from AWS; we will not issue a separate vendor invoice to Acme unless the listing is switched to "vendor-billed".

2) EU VAT (reverse-charge):
   - Because AWS invoices the customer, reverse-charge is not applied on a Redwood vendor invoice (there won't be one). However, Acme may still require evidence that the supply was marketplace-facilitated — we can provide the AWS invoice copy and the marketplace payout report as proof.

3) US (W-9):
   - For US entity purchases via marketplace, AWS handles tax. If Acme specifically requests Redwood to invoice them directly (vendor-billed), then yes — we require a completed W-9 before issuing a vendor invoice.

4) Deferred revenue / accounting impact:
   - For marketplace-facilitated sales, Redwood recognizes revenue on payouts received from the marketplace and may have timing differences compared to vendor-billed. For HS-82319 we should map the payout date to revenue recognition; procurement/finance of Acme shouldn't be impacted aside from receiving AWS's invoice.

Attachments I'm adding: AWS guidance on marketplace split (aws_marketplace_split_guidance.pdf) and a stub W-9 template we can send to Acme if they request direct invoicing.

Action items:
- Rajesh: please confirm whether Acme insists on a vendor invoice instead of AWS billing. If yes, send the legal entity details for the invoice and we'll forward the W-9 template for signature.
- Vanessa/Kimberly: if Acme needs a formal evidence packet (AWS invoice + payout report + Redwood cover note), Kimberly can prepare the tax cover note.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: aws_marketplace_split_guidance.pdf; W-9_template_filled_stub.pdf

Subject: Re: Invoice routing for upcoming co-sell (marketplace split & VAT)

Hi Rajesh — brief tax confirmation and a recommended one-page summary you can attach to the PO.

1) If AWS invoices Acme (marketplace-facilitated):
   - Acme receives the tax invoice from AWS. No Redwood vendor invoice is required.
   - For Acme Europe Ltd., AWS should apply the VAT rules; Acme can self-assess reverse-charge where applicable using the AWS invoice as support.

2) If Redwood needs to invoice (vendor-billed):
   - EU: we will issue a net invoice with billing reference to the PO and Acme's VAT ID. Acme should include a statement on the PO enabling reverse-charge (we can provide a short PO clause). We typically ask for a signed statement or a PO note confirming buyer will self-account for VAT. DocuSign is optional; a written PO note is usually sufficient.
   - US: Redwood requires a completed W-9 before payment processing if Redwood invoices directly.

3) Evidence packet (what Acme will receive if requested):
   - Copy of AWS invoice to Acme
   - Redwood payout report for the transaction
   - Redwood cover note explaining revenue split and confirming no vendor invoice was issued by Redwood for marketplace-facilitated sales
I attached a one-page summary (text below) you can paste into your PO and a stub W-9 if needed. Let me know if you want a DocuSign wrapper for the PO clause.

--- one-page summary (for Acme PO) ---
Redwood Inference: Marketplace co-sell billing summary- Transaction type: AWS Marketplace - Marketplace-facilitated sale- Invoice recipient: AWS (customer receives invoice from AWS)- VAT: AWS applies VAT per marketplace rules; buyer may self-assess reverse-charge using AWS invoice- Redwood documentation provided on request: AWS invoice copy, Redwood payout report, Redwood cover note- If vendor-billed is requested, provide Acme legal entity + VAT ID (EU) or W-9 (US) and Redwood will issue vendor invoice

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Tax & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
